title: Paraspinal Muscle Fatty Infiltration Is Associated With MRI-Defined Lumbar Fasciitis in Patients With Degenerative Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate the association between paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration and MRI-defined thoracolumbar fascial signal abnormalities in patients with degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis (DLSS). Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 303 patients with DLSS who underwent lumbar MRI between January 2024 and January 2026. MRI-defined thoracolumbar fascial signal abnormalities were identified on sagittal T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and fat-suppressed T2-weighted images. Paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration was assessed using a four-grade MRI-based classification and analyzed both dichotomously (Grades 1–2 vs. Grades 3–4) and as an ordinal variable. Relative cross-sectional areas of the erector spinae, multifidus, and psoas muscles were also measured. Factors associated with thoracolumbar fascial signal abnormalities were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to assess discriminative performance. Results MRI-defined thoracolumbar fascial signal abnormalities were present in 149 of 303 patients (49.2%). High-grade paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration was more frequent in patients with fascial signal abnormalities than in those without (P < 0.001). After adjustment for sex, diabetes mellitus, and relative psoas muscle cross-sectional area, high-grade fatty infiltration remained associated with higher odds of thoracolumbar fascial signal abnormalities (OR, 5.578; 95% CI, 3.325–9.357; P < 0.001). High-grade fatty infiltration alone yielded an AUC of 0.711 (95% CI, 0.660–0.761), whereas the multivariable model yielded an AUC of 0.741 (95% CI, 0.684–0.797). When fatty infiltration grade was modeled as an ordinal variable, each one-grade increase was associated with higher odds of fascial signal abnormalities (OR, 3.515; 95% CI, 2.383–5.185; P < 0.001), although the proportions across individual grades were not monotonically distributed. Conclusions In patients with degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis, high-grade paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration was associated with the presence of MRI-defined thoracolumbar fascial signal abnormalities. These findings suggest that paraspinal muscle composition and thoracolumbar fascial signal abnormalities may represent related imaging features of the posterior lumbar soft-tissue environment.

title: Complement C1q drives skeletal muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Abstract Cancer cachexia, defined by involuntary skeletal muscle loss, affects ~ 70% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients at diagnosis and independently worsens survival. Here, we identify complement component 1q (C1q) as a driver of PDAC-induced muscle wasting, with coordinated effects across muscle, tumor, and systemic inflammatory compartments. In cachectic PDAC patient muscle, C1q partially co-deposits with IgM, and C1q mRNA correlates with reduced muscle radiation attenuation, a CT-derived measure of muscle quality. In PDAC tumors, C1q protein correlates with immunosuppressive programs and independently predicts poor survival. These findings are recapitulated in orthotopic KPC mice, where C1q mRNA is upregulated in respiratory muscle before cachexia onset, and C1q deposits in tumors and co-deposits with IgM in muscles of cachectic mice. C1qa deletion reduced systemic inflammatory mediators, blocked muscle atrophy, and improved activity and grip strength in KPC mice, while attenuating immune cell infiltration and extracellular matrix remodeling in respiratory muscle. Host C1qa deletion also suppressed angiogenic and immunosuppressive programs in KPC tumors, while increasing intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell density and Granzyme B production. These findings position C1q as a driver of cancer-induced muscle wasting and tumor immunosuppression, supporting C1q inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy targeting pathological features of poor-prognosis PDAC.

title: Intraoperative Renal Biopsy During Liver Transplantation in Patients with Preexisting Acute Kidney Injury: Histopathological Associations with Postoperative Renal Replacement Therapy
abstract: Abstract Background. Acute kidney injury (AKI) in decompensated cirrhosis is associated with poor outcomes after liver transplantation (LT), and creatinine-based tools poorly predict postoperative renal recovery. We evaluated whether histopathology on intraoperative renal biopsy is associated with renal replacement therapy (RRT) after LT. Methods. In this retrospective single-center cohort study, 22 adults with decompensated cirrhosis and KDIGO-defined AKI underwent intraoperative renal biopsy during deceased-donor LT between October 2022 and June 2024. Two early deaths were retained in the safety cohort, leaving 20 patients for renal-outcome analysis. The primary endpoint was RRT within 90 days; prespecified histological predictors were acute tubular injury (ATI) score ≥ 2 and interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA) > 10%. Results. Five of 20 patients (25.0%) initiated RRT within 90 days, and 3 remained RRT-dependent at day 90. RRT occurred in 5 of 9 patients with ATI ≥ 2 versus 0 of 11 with ATI < 2 (risk difference, 55.6 percentage points; 95% CI, 16.8–81.1; P = .008) and in 4 of 7 with IFTA > 10% versus 1 of 13 with IFTA ≤ 10% (risk difference, 49.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 8.4–77.2; P = .031). IFTA correlated strongly with time to renal function stabilization (Spearman ρ = 0.907; P < .001). No severe biopsy-related complications occurred, although transient hematuria was common. No conventional preoperative clinical variable distinguished patients with and without subsequent RRT. Conclusions. Moderate-to-severe ATI and IFTA burden on intraoperative renal biopsy were associated with post-LT RRT requirement. Intraoperative biopsy was feasible in this high-risk population. These hypothesis-generating findings require validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices Toward Breast Cancer Among Nursing and Midwifery Students at the University of Health Sciences, Cambodia
abstract: Abstract Background Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among Cambodian women, with an estimated 2,116 new cases and 917 deaths in 2022. Nurses and midwives deliver most primary care in Cambodia, yet evidence on the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) of students in these professions toward breast cancer is lacking. This study assessed breast cancer KAP among nursing and midwifery students in Cambodia. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in November 2024 among 705 students enrolled in four nursing and midwifery programmes at the University of Health Sciences, Phnom Penh. A structured, self-administered 50-item questionnaire assessed knowledge (25 items), attitudes (16 items) and breast self-examination (BSE) practice (3 items). Data were analysed using Pearson’s chi-square tests, Welch two-sample t-tests, one-way analysis of variance and Pearson correlation. Results Overall, 73.3% of students had adequate knowledge, 99.7% held positive attitudes and 85.2% were classified as having good BSE practice. Knowledge, attitude and practice scores differed significantly by year of study (p < 0.001), with mean knowledge scores increasing from 13.9 in Year 1 to 19.7 in Year 4. Knowledge and attitude scores did not differ between programmes, whereas midwifery students more often reported practising BSE than nursing students (88.2% vs. 66.4%, p < 0.001). Only 45.1% had heard of mammography and 56.3% recognised a painless lump as a warning sign, while 48.1% believed that breast cancer is fatal for all patients. Knowledge correlated moderately with attitude (r = 0.425) and practice (r = 0.400) (both p < 0.001). Conclusions Nursing and midwifery students held favourable attitudes toward early detection, but important gaps persisted in mammography awareness, recognition of a painless lump as a warning sign and identification of hormonal and lifestyle risk factors. Integrating structured breast health education, including clinical breast examination skills, early in pre-service curricula may strengthen the capacity of this workforce to support early detection of breast cancer in Cambodia.

title: Sequential integration of pre-discharge lung ultrasound and the MEESSI-AHF score for safe emergency department discharge in decompensated heart failure: a prospective multicentre cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Early revisit or readmission is common after direct emergency department (ED) discharge for decompensated heart failure (DHF, previously termed acute heart failure). We evaluated whether pre-discharge lung ultrasound, quantified as the number of lung fields with B-lines (NLFB-L), improves 30-day risk stratification, alone or integrated with the Multiple Estimation of Risk based on the Emergency department Spanish Score in patients with Acute Heart Failure (MEESSI-AHF). Methods Prospective multicentre cohort study of 96 adults with DHF discharged directly from the EDs of four Spanish tertiary hospitals between November 2023 and January 2026. The primary outcome was heart failure-related ED revisit or hospital readmission within 30 days. Associations were assessed with logistic regression (two-variable models), discrimination with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) compared by the DeLong test, and the optimal NLFB-L threshold with the Youden index. A sequential strategy stratified risk by pre-discharge congestion (NLFB-L < 5 vs ≥ 5), refined by baseline MEESSI-AHF category (low vs non-low). Results The primary outcome occurred in 26 patients (27.1%). NLFB-L was independently associated with the outcome after adjustment for natriuretic peptide levels (adjusted odds ratio 1.51 per additional lung field; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.21–1.90; p < 0.001). NLFB-L discriminated better than the MEESSI-AHF score (AUC 0.849 vs 0.670; DeLong p = 0.0037), whereas combining both did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.853; p = 0.953). The optimal threshold was NLFB-L ≥ 5 (69.2% sensitivity, 82.9% specificity, 87.9% negative predictive value). NLFB-L < 5 carried a 12.1% event rate; among patients with NLFB-L ≥ 5, event rates were 35.7% with low-risk and 81.3% with non-low-risk MEESSI-AHF (odds ratio 31.42 versus NLFB-L < 5, 95% CI 7.32–134.85; p < 0.001). Conclusions Pre-discharge NLFB-L strongly predicted 30-day heart failure-related revisit or readmission. The added value of the MEESSI-AHF score emerged with sequential integration: a non-low MEESSI-AHF category refined prognosis only in patients with persistent congestion; when both are present, direct ED discharge should be reconsidered. Trial registration: Not applicable (observational study, not registered).

title: Tau PET in tauopathies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of regional tau deposition and diagnostic performance
abstract: Abstract Background Tauopathies represent a diverse group of neurodegenerative diseases characterized by abnormal tau protein aggregation. Accurate differential diagnosis remains challenging due to overlapping clinical features and the limited specificity of conventional imaging. Tau positron emission tomography (PET) imaging represents a promising diagnostic tool for tauopathies. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to examine regional uptake patterns and assess the diagnostic performance of tau PET across major tauopathies. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to evaluate regional tau deposition and the diagnostic performance of tau PET. Regional tau tracer uptake values and diagnostic accuracy parameters (sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve [AUC]) were analyzed using random effects models to estimate standardized mean differences (SMD) and pooled diagnostic performance, respectively. Results Compared with HCs, patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) had significantly elevated tau uptake in 27 brain regions (SMD range: 0.39–2.58; p < 0.01), patients with progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) in eight regions (0.41–1.71; p < 0.05), and patients with corticobasal syndrome (CBS) in four regions (1.06–1.86; p < 0.01). The pooled AUCs for distinguishing AD, PSP, and AD/mild cognitive impairment (MCI) patients from HCs were 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89–0.96), 0.92 (0.85–0.99), and 0.84 (0.74–0.94), respectively. Subgroup analyses revealed differences in tau uptake and diagnostic accuracy by outcome type, atlas application, tracer type, and generation. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate that tau PET reveals disease-specific uptake patterns with high diagnostic accuracy across tauopathies. The distinct spatial distributions of AD, PSP, and CBS provide valuable neuroimaging signatures for differential diagnosis. These results support the use of tau PET as a promising clinical biomarker, although methodological standardization is essential for optimal implementation.

title: Pretreatment CT-based clinical deep learning radiomics model for predicting the response of hepatocellular carcinoma patients with portal vein thrombosis treated with TKIs plus PD-1 inhibitors and hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to construct a pretreatment contrast-enhanced CT (CECT)-based multimodal model for noninvasive forecasting of early treatment response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients with portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) who received hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy combined with tyrosine kinase inhibitors and PD-1 inhibitors (HTI). Methods We retrospectively enrolled 116 patients with HCC and PVTT receiving HTIs (2019–2024), randomly divided 7:3 into training (n = 81) and test (n = 35) cohorts. Early objective response was assessed 6–8 weeks after treatment using modified RECIST. Radiomic features were extracted from three-dimensional volumes of interest of the primary tumor and PVTT; deep features from the largest axial tumor slice using ResNet101. Six models were developed; the final radiomic–deep learning–clinical (RCLD) model integrated out-of-fold component probabilities. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and overall survival (OS) stratification were evaluated. Results Sixty-eight patients responded (complete response, n = 3; partial response, n = 65); the objective response rate was 58.6% and disease control rate 91.4%. Four radiomic and three deep learning features were selected; cirrhosis was the only clinical variable. RCLD achieved the highest AUC (training 0.965, 95% CI 0.929–1.000; test 0.924, 95% CI 0.822–1.000). In the test cohort, RCLD outperformed clinical-only and radiomics–clinical models ( p = 0.003 and p = 0.026), with no significant differences from other imaging-based models. RCLD stratified OS (training P = 0.003; test P = 0.027). Conclusion A pretreatment CECT-based multimodal model integrating radiomics, deep learning, and cirrhosis predicted early objective response and stratified OS risk in HCC with PVTT receiving HTIs. Prospective multicenter validation is required.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Automated Detection and Segmentation of Pulp Stones in Cone Beam Computed Tomography Scans.
abstract: Abstract Objective : This study aimed to automatically detect the human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stones on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) using deep learning-based semantic segmentation. Methodology : 523 annotated images of teeth from 112 CBCT examinations were used to train and evaluate four established deep learning architectures (U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and DeepLabV3+) in segmenting the background, pulp cavity, and pulp stone(s). Subsequently a novel architecture was developed (DACA-DeepLab) and evaluated through an additive study. DACA-DeepLab incorporates DeepLabV3+ with a pyramid channel-spatial attention (PCSA) module, a dual-axis cross-attention (DACA) decoder, and a Sobel-guided boundary-refinement (BFR) head. Results : DeepLabV3+ achieved the best overall Dice performance among the four baseline architectures (mean, 0.775; pulp cavity, 0.838; pulp stone, 0.711). In the second study, combining PCSA and DACA yielded the highest performance (mean Dice, 0.733). Adding the boundary-refinement head reduced performance, suggesting sensitivity to the limited training set. title: Anatomical classification and operative strategy for bilateral congenital lung lesions in children: a consecutive series of eight patients with a review of the literature
abstract: Abstract Purpose Bilateral congenital lung lesions are rare and no operative framework exists. We describe the anatomical patterns and how they determine operative decisions. Methods Of 660 consecutive resections for congenital lung lesions (September 2019 to July 2026), eight children (1.2%) had lesions in both hemithoraces on contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT). Lesions were continuous when a structure linked the two sides anterior to the spine, and separate when independent. Results Two patients had continuous lesions, one linked by an arterial trunk from the abdominal aorta and one by an extralobar sequestration crossing the midline; both were resected through one pleural cavity. Of the six with separate lesions, four met an indication on both sides and were operated in two stages 6.7 to 16.4 months apart; in two the contralateral lesion (4.5 and 13 mm) was observed. All 12 operations were completed thoracoscopically without conversion, transfusion or complication, and no new contralateral lesion appeared over a median follow-up of 32 months. Conclusion The first question is whether a structure links the two sides anterior to the spine. If so, both sides can be resected through one pleural cavity; if not, each side is judged on its own indication and staged resection preferred.

title: Exploratory Biomarker and Imaging Outcome Signals in the Singaporean Trial of CN‑105 Treatment for Acute Supratentorial Intracerebral Hemorrhage (S-CATCH) ​
abstract: Abstract Background/Objective : CN-105 is an apolipoprotein E-mimetic pentapeptide designed to attenuate neuroinflammation after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). This exploratory secondary analysis of the Singaporean Trial of CN-105 Treatment for Acute Supratentorial Intracerebral Hemorrhage (S-CATCH) evaluated plasma and imaging biomarkers in relation to functional outcome and treatment response. Methods S-CATCH was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2b trial of CN-105 in 60 patients with acute primary supratentorial ICH. Serial plasma protein concentrations and computed tomography measurements were evaluated for associations with 30- and 90-day modified Rankin Scale outcomes. Treatment-associated trajectories were expressed as CN-105:placebo ratios of geometric mean fold changes from baseline. Perihematomal edema was evaluated using the edema:blood volume (E:BV) ratio. Results Higher interleukin-6, D-dimer, C-reactive protein, S100 calcium-binding protein B, and B-type natriuretic peptide concentrations were associated with worse functional outcomes in unadjusted analyses. CN-105 was associated with smaller geometric mean fold changes in D-dimer on day 1 (ratio 0.644; p = 0.042) and vascular endothelial growth factor on day 2 (ratio 0.777; p = 0.012). Overall imaging models containing baseline D-dimer, tumor necrosis factor-α, or vascular endothelial growth factor, treatment arm, and their interaction were significant on individual scan days. P-values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Conclusions CN-105 was not significantly associated with functional outcome. D-dimer showed exploratory outcome- and treatment-associated signals warranting further validation as a candidate prognostic and pharmacodynamic marker. Clinical Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03711903. Registered October 16, 2018. https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03711903?term=NCT03711903&rank=1

title: A Decoder-Free Soft-Token Segmenter for Point-of-Care Breast Ultrasound
abstract: Abstract Purpose :Automatic lesion localization can support point-of-care breast ultrasound (US), where operators often have limited training and scanners have limited compute and memory. Most segmentation models pair a pretrained encoder with a learned decoder, which adds parameters and computational cost. We propose a decoder-free soft-token segmenter that supervises each vision transformer (ViT) patch token with the fraction of lesion pixels in its patch. Methods :A layer normalization and a single linear layer map each token to one logit, and the resulting grid is upsampled bilinearly to image resolution. We evaluated three encoder sizes and two initializations on the public BUS-BRA test set, both in-domain and out-of-domain, against five fully fine-tuned models with feature pyramid network (FPN) decoders. Results :An oracle analysis showed that soft targets at patch size 8 raise the best achievable Dice to 0.970. The ViT-Tiny model, with 5.53 million parameters and a 577-parameter head, reached an in-domain Dice of 0.869 at 1,257 images/s, compared with 0.909 at 74 images/s for the most accurate FPN model DINOv2. Most of the remaining gap came from small lesions, where the model extended its mask into adjacent hypoechoic tissue, while low lesion contrast degraded all models similarly. Conclusion :These results support decoder-free soft-token segmentation as an efficient lesion localizer for resource-constrained breast US.

title: Development and characterization of FI 7500: a novel near-infrared dye for in vitro and in vivo cell labeling
abstract: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent dyes offer considerable advantages over visible-light fluorescent dyes for in vivo imaging, including reduced tissue scattering and superior penetration depth. Current in vivo imaging in small animals predominantly relies on bioluminescence imaging using luciferase-expressing cells, which requires genetic modification and repeated substrate administration. However, only a few NIR fluorescent dyes have been sufficiently validated for in vivo applications. Here, we present a comprehensive characterization of the NIR fluorescent dye FI 7500 as a practical alternative to bioluminescence imaging. Microscopy-based analysis revealed that FI 7500 specifically localizes to the cytoplasm across multiple cell types, enabling clear visualization of cellular morphology in both two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) culture models. In 3D spheroid imaging, FI 7500 visualized the internal structures of live spheroids containing up to 2×10 3 cells, and optical clearing extended visualization to spheroids containing 1×10 4 cells. Furthermore, FI 7500 enabled clear surface imaging and delineation of individual cells regardless of spheroid size. In vivo, subcutaneously transplanted FI 7500-stained cells retained fluorescence for up to 21 days, with minimal effects on tumor growth. After intravenous administration, FI 7500-stained lung-metastasizing cells accumulated in the lungs, consistent with the bioluminescence signal after luciferin administration. These findings support the use of FI 7500 as a versatile and reliable tool for cellular and in vivo imaging, expanding the choice of validated NIR dyes and providing essential data to guide probe selection for specific experimental applications.

title: Association of Preoperative CT-Derived Intratumoral Heterogeneity with Recurrence Risk in Completely Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background: Intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is closely associated with prognosis, while the quantitative parameters currently used for non-invasive characterization of ITH remained to provide only limited information. To compare the prognostic value of preoperative CT-derived ITH versus habitat heterogeneity score (HHS) for disease-free survival (DFS) in resected NSCLC, and to assess the incremental value of HHS and its association with adjuvant chemotherapy benefit. Methods: This retrospective study included 631 patients with stage I–IIIA NSCLC who underwent curative-intent resection; the endpoint was 3-year DFS. ITH was quantified from the largest axial tumor section, whereas HHS was constructed via voxel-level radiophenotypic clustering across the whole tumor volume. Prognostic performance was assessed using multivariable Cox regression, the concordance index, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). A 1:1 propensity score matching analysis in patients with stage II–IIIA disease evaluated the interaction between HHS and adjuvant chemotherapy. Results: Recurrence or death occurred in 186 patients within 3 years. ITH was not significantly associated with DFS, whereas HHS remained an independent prognostic factor (hazard ratio=2.27, P<0.001) and stratified recurrence risk within stage I, II, and IIIA subgroups. Incorporating HHS into the clinicopathological model yielded a nomogram with concordance index of 0.80 and an AUC of 0.87, significantly outperforming the TNM and clinicopathological models. In the matched cohort, HHS interacted significantly with adjuvant chemotherapy (P for interaction=0.031); chemotherapy conferred a DFS benefit across both heterogeneity strata, with a greater relative risk reduction in the low-HHS group. Conclusions: HHS independently predicts DFS and refines risk stratification in resectable NSCLC, serving as a promising noninvasive biomarker for prognostic assessment and personalized adjuvant chemotherapy decisions.

title: Cerebellum–white-matter proportionality is associated with cognition but not explained by lobular anatomy
abstract: Abstract Background. A previously identified association between whole-cerebellum and cerebral-white-matter (Cer:WM) allocation and cognitive ability does not establish a lobular mechanism. We tested whether this association in Amsterdam Open MRI Collection (AOMIC) ID1000 was robust to a new cerebellar measurement and explained by regional allocation. Methods. First-run T1-weighted scans from 928 participants were processed outcome-blind with FastSurfer/CerebNet v2.6.0. Before regional measurements were joined to cognition, the primary exposure was fixed as the log ratio of bilateral Crus I, Crus II and VIIb to bilateral lobules I-IV and V. Blinded quality control produced one anatomical exclusion; final analyses used 925 participants and adjusted for age, sex, tissue scale and five-part macroanatomical composition. Results. The newly measured Cer:WM association remained positive (standardized β = 0.101, 95% CI 0.029–0.174, p=.0063; old/new cerebellar totals r=.982). The locked posterior:anterior ratio was null (β = 0.004, 95% CI -0.059-0.067, p=.908); its confidence interval excluded standardized effects of magnitude ≥ 0.067, and a post-hoc equivalence test supported equivalence within ± 0.10 (TOST p=.0014). The regional term attenuated the baseline macro Cer:WM coefficient by only 0.28%. Global lobular-composition and asymmetry tests were null, and regional augmentation was uninformative in cross-validation. Conclusions. The AOMIC Cer:WM association is robust to cerebellar measurement method but is not explained by detectable lobular allocation in healthy young adults. Cerebral white matter and cerebellum showed markedly different intracranial-volume scaling (exponents 0.606 versus 0.372), underscoring allometric and compositional specification as an important benchmark for cerebellar morphometry.

title: Multidisciplinary perioperative management of emergency laparoscopic appendectomy for perforated appendicitis in a child with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) are vulnerable to anesthesia-associated rhabdomyolysis-like events, hyperkalemia, postoperative respiratory failure, and occult cardiomyopathy. These risks complicate emergency abdominal surgery, where delayed source control may worsen sepsis. Detailed pediatric perioperative reports describing multidisciplinary risk mitigation for emergency abdominal surgery in DMD remain extremely limited, and practical clinical pathways are lacking. Case presentation: A 9-year-old Han Chinese ambulatory boy with genetically confirmed DMD (exon 51 deletion) presented with 40 hours of right lower quadrant pain, peritoneal irritation, a fecalith on ultrasound, markedly elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein 186.84 mg/L), and elevated creatine kinase (5139 U/L). Focused preoperative cardiopulmonary assessment showed preserved left ventricular systolic function and no biochemical evidence of acute myocardial injury. An urgent multidisciplinary meeting involving pediatric surgery, anesthesiology, pediatric intensive care, neurology, and endocrinology was convened within 6 hours of admission. Hybrid single-incision laparoscopic appendectomy with an additional 5-mm assisting trocar was performed under non-trigger total intravenous anesthesia, with strict avoidance of succinylcholine and volatile anesthetic agents, serial arterial blood gas and potassium monitoring, perioperative steroid bridging, readiness for malignant hyperthermia-like deterioration including immediate availability of dantrolene, and planned postoperative pediatric intensive care unit admission. Intraoperative findings confirmed perforated gangrenous appendicitis with diffuse purulent peritonitis. The patient was extubated shortly after PICU arrival, developed no perioperative hyperkalemia, arrhythmia, pigmenturia, or MH-like hypermetabolic signs, and recovered uneventfully after staged antibiotic therapy. Conclusions: This case illustrates a practical perioperative pathway for emergency abdominal surgery in a selected ambulatory child with DMD and supports timely minimally invasive source control when perioperative risk mitigation is protocolized. However, it should not be interpreted as a representative model for all patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, particularly those with advanced cardiopulmonary impairment or more complex airway and metabolic risk profiles.

title: Bleeding Complications Following Image-Guided Kidney Biopsy: A Single-Center Experience
abstract: Abstract Purpose Compare clinically significant bleeding rates across native, transplant, and renal mass image-guided biopsies; characterize bleeding timing to guide post-procedure monitoring; and identify associated patient and procedural factors. Methods A radiology information system search identified all image-guided renal biopsies by the abdominal imaging section from 01/01/2021 to 04/01/2025. Data included demographics, laboratory values, procedural parameters, and intra- and post-procedure bleeding findings. Clinically significant bleeding was defined by post-procedure CT showing active extravasation or moderate/large hematoma, or intervention to control bleeding. Results The cohort comprised 1,255 biopsies (508 native, 615 transplant, 132 renal mass), with clinically significant bleeding in 45 (3.6%). Native kidneys bled nearly three times more often than transplants (5.7% [29/508] vs. 2.0% [12/615]; OR, 3.04; p = .001) and required more interventions (4.1% [21/508] vs. 0.8% [5/615]; p < .001); the renal mass rate (3.0% [4/132]) did not differ significantly from either. Detection was temporally distributed: 42.2% of events occurred within 2 hours, 8.9% between 2–6 hours, 24.4% between 6–24 hours, and 24.4% beyond 24 hours. On multivariable analysis of pre-procedural factors, biopsy target (p = .02), platelet count (p = .003), and systolic blood pressure (p = .04) independently predicted bleeding; female sex showed a borderline association (p = .051). Conclusion Higher bleeding risk of native over transplant biopsy persisted after adjustment for baseline patient factors. Bleeding events clustered within 2 hours (42%) or beyond 24 hours (24%), and most events detected after leaving the biopsy suite were prompted by patient-reportable rather than monitoring-dependent symptoms.

title: Value of 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics combined with clinical features for predicting Ki-67 expression in colorectal cancer
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics combined with clinical features for the preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression in colorectal cancer (CRC). Methods A total of 117 patients with pathologically confirmed CRC who underwent pretreatment 18F-FDG PET/CT between June 2016 and October 2024 were retrospectively included. Patients were classified into high- and low-expression groups using a 50% Ki-67 cutoff and were randomly divided into a training cohort and an internal validation cohort at a 7:3 ratio. Radiomic features were extracted from CT and PET images and reduced by standardization, univariate screening, correlation analysis, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), ExtraTrees, LightGBM, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers were compared. Independent clinical predictors were identified to construct a clinical model and a combined clinical-radiomics nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, the DeLong test, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Six CT features, four PET features, and ten combined PET/CT features were retained. TNM stage, SUVmax, and SUVmean were independent predictors of high Ki-67 expression. The LightGBM-based PET/CT radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.943 and 0.911 in the training and internal validation cohorts, respectively, with an accuracy of 0.861 in the validation cohort. The combined nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.951 and 0.913, with validation-cohort accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score of 0.917, 0.920, 0.909, and 0.939, respectively. The AUC difference between the combined model and the PET/CT radiomics model was not statistically significant, whereas DCA showed a higher net benefit for the combined model within part of the clinically relevant threshold range. Conclusion Multimodal 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics characterizes CRC from complementary morphologic and metabolic perspectives. Combining radiomics with TNM stage and conventional metabolic parameters may improve preoperative identification of high Ki-67 expression. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), ExtraTrees, LightGBM, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers were compared. Independent clinical predictors were identified to construct a clinical model and a combined clinical-radiomics nomogram. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, the DeLong test, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Six CT features, four PET features, and ten combined PET/CT features were retained. TNM stage, SUVmax, and SUVmean were independent predictors of high Ki-67 expression. The LightGBM-based PET/CT radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.943 and 0.911 in the training and internal validation cohorts, respectively, with an accuracy of 0.861 in the validation cohort. The combined nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.951 and 0.913, with validation-cohort accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score of 0.917, 0.920, 0.909, and 0.939, respectively. The AUC difference between the combined model and the PET/CT radiomics model was not statistically significant, whereas DCA showed a higher net benefit for the combined model within part of the clinically relevant threshold range. Conclusion Multimodal 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics characterizes CRC from complementary morphologic and metabolic perspectives. Combining radiomics with TNM stage and conventional metabolic parameters may improve preoperative identification of high Ki-67 expression. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Diagnostic yield of Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) guided Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) in peripheral pulmonary infections: a prospective pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is a key diagnostic tool in evaluating pulmonary infections and infiltrative lung diseases. However, conventional BAL relies on operator-dependent segment selection, potentially limiting diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions. Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) has been shown to improve localization in biopsy procedures but its role in guiding BAL remains unexplored. Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic yield of VBN-guided BAL in patients with clinical features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. Methods: This prospective observational pilot study included 50 adult patients with features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. All patients underwent VBN-guided BAL. Samples were analyzed using microbiological, molecular, and cytological techniques. Diagnostic yield and impact on clinical diagnosis were assessed. Results: A definitive diagnosis was achieved in 42/50 patients (84%). Diagnostic yield was higher in immunocompromised patients (92.9%) compared to non-immunocompromised patients (80.6%), though not statistically significant (p=0.414). The final diagnosis differed from the initial clinical diagnosis in 62% of cases. Common diagnoses included bacterial pneumonia (36%), tuberculosis (28%), and fungal infections (16%). Conclusion: VBN-guided BAL demonstrates high diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions and may significantly alter clinical management. Larger comparative studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Analysis of Risk Factors and Establishment of a Predictive Model for Endplate Collapse After Posterior Short-Segment Fixation Combined with Screw Placement at the Injured Vertebra in Thoracolumbar Fractures
abstract: Abstract Purpose To identify the risk factors for endplate collapse in patients with thoracolumbar fractures undergoing posterior short-segment fixation combined with intermediate screw placement, and to develop and validate a clinical prediction model to aid in early risk stratification and prognosis optimization. Materials and methods Clinical data from 135 patients with thoracolumbar fractures treated with posterior short-segment fixation and screw placement at the injured vertebra were retrospectively analyzed. Based on postoperative imaging findings, patients were stratified into an endplate collapse group (n = 57) and a non-collapse control group (n = 78). Variables collected included demographic and fracture characteristics (age, gender, BMI, fracture location, fracture pattern, mechanism of injury, osteoporotic status), radiographic parameters (screw length at the injured vertebra, severity of endplate and intervertebral disc injury, extent of anterior and posterior complex injury, postoperative mean vertebral body height [MVBH] and Cobb angle [CA]), and postoperative outcomes (fixation duration, postoperative Pfirrmann grade). Univariate analysis identified variables with significant between-group differences. Independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse were determined by multivariable logistic regression analysis. A predictive model was constructed incorporating these factors, and its performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with calculation of area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results Univariate analysis revealed significant differences in BMI, osteoporotic status, screw depth, endplate injury grade, intervertebral disc injury severity (Sander classification), load-sharing classification (LSC) score, postoperative Pfirrmann grade, and postoperative Cobb angle between groups (all P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade as independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse (all P < 0.05), with screw depth demonstrating the largest odds ratio and thus the strongest association. A predictive model incorporating these three factors was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888 (95% CI: 0.826–0.943), with sensitivity of 78.9% and specificity of 89.7%, indicating favorable predictive performance. Conclusion Postoperative endplate collapse following posterior short-segment fixation with injured vertebra screw placement for thoracolumbar fractures is multifactorial, with osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade serving as major independent risk factors. The predictive model developed in this study effectively stratifies the risk of postoperative endplate collapse and may provide a valuable tool for preoperative risk assessment, intraoperative technical optimization, and postoperative individualized rehabilitation planning, thereby potentially reducing the incidence of endplate collapse and improving functional outcomes.

title: Gastric adenocarcinoma of fundic-gland mucosa type incidentally detected during endoscopy for upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Gastric adenocarcinoma of fundic-gland mucosa type (GA-FGM) is a rare gastric epithelial neoplasm that can be challenging to diagnose before resection because of its subtle endoscopic features and relatively mild cytological atypia. We report a case of GA-FGM incidentally detected during endoscopy for upper gastrointestinal bleeding, highlighting the importance of careful endoscopic examination and histopathological evaluation. Case presentation: A 59-year-old man was admitted with hematemesis and melena. Emergency gastroscopy revealed a bleeding gastric antral ulcer and an incidental reddish elevated lesion measuring 2.5 × 3.0 cm on the posterior wall of the upper gastric body. Image-enhanced endoscopy demonstrated abnormal superficial vascular patterns and subtle mucosal changes. Endoscopic ultrasonography suggested that the lesion originated from the mucosa and extended into the muscularis propria. Biopsy findings raised suspicion of GA-FGM. Although surgical gastrectomy was recommended, the patient declined and underwent endoscopic resection. Histopathological examination confirmed GA-FGM, with invasion reaching the muscularis propria and reported lymphovascular invasion. Both horizontal and vertical resection margins were negative. Additional gastrectomy was recommended because of the invasive features, but the patient declined further surgery. Conclusion GA-FGM may be incidentally detected during endoscopic evaluation for unrelated gastrointestinal conditions and may present with subtle mucosal abnormalities despite deep tumor invasion. Careful assessment of endoscopic findings and comprehensive histopathological examination are essential for diagnosis and treatment planning. Deep invasion and lymphovascular involvement warrant consideration of additional treatment, even when resection margins are negative.

title: A Retrospective Comparative Study of 3-Month Early Outcomes Between L-Unitary Soft Endoscopy-Assisted Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion and Conventional Open Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion for Single-Level Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the 3-month early clinical outcomes of L-Unitary Soft Endoscopy (LUSE)-assisted anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) versus conventional open ACDF in the treatment of single-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM), and to evaluate the perioperative safety and early feasibility of LUSE-assisted ACDF, thereby providing a reference for clinical decision-making. Methods A retrospective comparative study was conducted on patients with single-level CSM who underwent ACDF at our hospital between January 2025 and June 2026. Patients were divided into two groups according to the surgical approach: the LUSE-assisted ACDF group (Group A) and the conventional open ACDF group (Group B). Perioperative parameters (operative time, intraoperative blood loss, incision length, length of hospital stay, and perioperative complications) were recorded. The Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) score, JOA improvement rate, and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores for overall neck/shoulder pain were assessed preoperatively and at 3 months postoperatively and compared between the two groups. The 1-month postoperative assessment was used primarily for safety monitoring. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS 27.0. Results A total of 63 patients were enrolled, including 30 in Group A and 33 in Group B. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups in baseline characteristics, including age, sex, height, weight, BMI, and affected segment (P > 0.05). Compared with Group B, Group A had a significantly shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss, and a shorter incision length (P < 0.05). No statistically significant difference was found in length of hospital stay between the two groups (P > 0.05). At 3 months postoperatively, both groups showed significant improvements in JOA scores, JOA improvement rates, and VAS scores for overall neck/shoulder pain compared with preoperative values (P < 0.05), with no statistically significant between-group differences in any of these outcomes (P > 0.05).No severe complications occurred in either group during the 1-month safety monitoring period, and the difference in complication rates was not statistically significant (P > 0.05). Conclusion Compared with conventional open ACDF, LUSE-assisted ACDF for single-level CSM showed no statistically significant difference in early neurological improvement at 3 months, while offering advantages including a smaller incision, less intraoperative blood loss, and a shorter operative time. These findings indicate that LUSE-assisted ACDF is technically feasible and safe in this preliminary series.

title: Knowledge-guided artificial intelligence supports radiographic surgical planning for acetabular reconstruction in developmental hip dysplasia
abstract: Abstract Acetabular planning for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) commonly uses two-dimensional templating or CT-based workflows. We developed Knowledge-base-guided Acetabular Planning for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip (KAP-DDH), which integrates automated two-dimensional radiographic analysis with paired historical surgical reconstructions to generate patient-specific plans. In this retrospective two-centre study, development, internal-validation and external-validation cohorts comprised 2,760, 691 and 422 records. Evaluation used two expert references and two blinded surgeon planners. External cup-diameter mean absolute errors were 3.18 mm for KAP-DDH, 4.37 mm for Surgeon 1 and 3.25 mm for Surgeon 2; both surgeons had smaller errors internally. Historical-case guidance reduced cup-diameter error by 0.54 mm internally and 0.62 mm externally versus Crowe-specific defaults and reduced positional errors, with little change in inclination or coverage errors. All evaluated KAP-DDH plans met prespecified inclination and coverage criteria. These findings support translating historical reconstruction experience into patient-specific radiographic planning targets.

title: Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy and Metabolic MRI in Epilepsy: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Synthesis of Neurochemical Biomarkers and Clinical Applications
abstract: Abstract Background: Since the introduction of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹H-MRS) in epilepsy research in the 1980s, metabolic MRI has provided unique insights into the neurochemical alterations underlying epilepsy. However, evidence has remained fragmented across imaging modalities, epilepsy syndromes, and clinical applications. We systematically reviewed the literature to define the metabolic phenotype of epilepsy and evaluate the evolving role of metabolic MRI in epilepsy research and clinical practice. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed and Scopus were systematically searched through April 2026 for original human studies investigating metabolic MRI in epilepsy. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. Findings were synthesized through structured qualitative evidence, supported by integrated methodological, scientometric, tabular, and visual analyses. Results: A total of 298 studies were included. Focal epilepsy demonstrated widespread alterations involving N-acetyl aspartate, glutamate, Gamma-aminobutyric acid, choline-containing compounds, myo-inositol, lactate, and other metabolites across epileptogenic and brain networks. Generalized epilepsy was characterized by predominantly bilateral and thalamo-cortical metabolic abnormalities, whereas tumor-associated epilepsy showed distinct metabolic alterations within tumors and the peritumoral zone. Treatment and prognostic studies demonstrated metabolite-specific changes following pharmacological and surgical interventions, and emerging metabolic MRI techniques provided complementary information on bioenergetics, ionic homeostasis, glutamatergic cycling, and metabolic flux. Conclusions: The available evidence supports epilepsy as a disorder of distributed metabolic networks that share a common signature of neuronal dysfunction while exhibiting syndrome-specific alterations in neurotransmission, gliosis, and energy metabolism. Complementary metabolic MRI techniques provide distinct biological information, but their clinical translation will require methodological harmonization and multimodal integration.

title: Endoscopic fenestration and Endoscope-Guided Placement of Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt with additional side holes for Multiloculated Hydrocephalus: A Technical Note
abstract: Abstract Multiloculated hydrocephalus (MLH) is characterized by multiple non-communicating cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartments and is associated with disproportionately high rates of shunt malfunction and revision surgery. We describe, in a stepwise technical format, an approach combining endoscopic cystoventriculostomy (inter-loculation fenestration) with endoscope-guided ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt catheter placement in an infant with multiloculated hydrocephalus. A 10-month-old male infant presented with progressive macrocephaly and developmental delay. Preoperative TORCH serology was notable for positive Rubella IgM and IgG, supporting a congenital rubella infection. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multiple variable-sized loculated cysts (largest 30 × 39 mm) in the interhemispheric, bilateral parietal, and left temporal regions with mass effect on dilated lateral ventricles, in keeping with multiloculated hydrocephalus of probable post-infectious/congenital origin. A rigid neuroendoscope was used to sequentially fenestrate the intraventricular septa, and a single ventricular catheter, modified with additional side ports, was then advanced under direct endoscopic vision into the fenestrated common cavity. Wide endoscopic communication was established between the previously isolated loculations. A formal endoscopic third ventriculostomy was deliberately not attempted in this case because the distorted, loculated anatomy rendered safe access to the third ventricular floor unfavourable, compounded by the patient's young age and the extent of supratentorial multiloculation, which already necessitated shunt placement. The ventricular catheter tip and side holes were confirmed endoscopically to lie freely within the fenestrated cavity, away from choroid plexus and septal remnants, with free CSF drainage confirmed prior to closure. Postoperative CT confirmed marked decompression of the previously multiloculated cysts into a single residual cavity traversed by the catheter, without hemorrhage or new isolated loculation. Endoscopic fenestration combined with endoscope-guided, side-hole-modified catheter placement is a feasible and reproducible technique that allows direct, real-time confirmation of catheter position within a fenestrated common cavity. This may reduce the risk of isolated-compartment recurrence that complicates freehand or purely image-guided catheter placement in multiloculated hydrocephalus, although larger comparative series and longer follow-up are required.

title: CardioJEPA: A Framework for Holistic Cardiac Representations Through Predictive Multimodal Alignment with ECG-Preservation
abstract: Abstract The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used cardiac diagnostic tool, but it reflects cardiac structure and function only indirectly. Aligning ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) representations offers a way to transfer imaging-derived structural knowledge into the ECG encoder without compromising the electrophysiological information it already carries. Contrastive learning has become the predominant approach for ECG--CMR alignment, yet the quality of the learned representation is jointly determined by the CMR target representation, the alignment objective, and the preservation of electrophysiological information unique to the ECG. We propose CardioJEPA, a predictive alignment framework built on frozen cardiac foundation models that addresses all three: a target that separates static anatomy from cardiac motion, a predictive objective that maps ECG representations onto a fixed CMR target without instance discrimination, and a preservation term that retains nearly all pre-alignment electrophysiological information. On 63,193 paired ECG--CMR recordings from the UK Biobank, CardioJEPA outperforms previous ECG--CMR alignment methods across structural, electrical, and diagnostic tasks, retains 98.6% of the ECG-unique information present before alignment, substantially reduces the modality gap relative to matched contrastive alignment, and transfers to external cohorts for structural heart disease and Chagas cardiomyopathy without task-specific training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Anatomically-Guided Attention for False Positive Reduction in Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract U-Net-based brain tumor segmentation can produce false positives in anatomically implausible locations, which inflate tumor volume estimates and reduce clinical trust. We investigate whether injecting an anatomical location prior into the network's attention can reduce these errors. We propose a prior informed attention gate that conditions U-Net features on empirical tumor-location prior maps computed from the training annotations, applied as a residual spatial gate at the bottleneck and at every decoder stage. Using the BRISC dataset of 2D contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI slices (glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor), we compare the proposed model with a vanilla U-Net and a learned-gate ablation under identical training, using 3-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set of 860 images. We evaluate Dice, IoU, precision, recall, Hausdorff distance, HD95 and a dedicated far false-positive measure. The proposed model matched the baseline in Dice (0.709 versus 0.708) and showed a slightly lower but non-significant HD95 (36.5 versus 37.9 px, p = 0.26); it did not significantly reduce far false positives (49.7 versus 48.0 px, p = 0.82). A simple location prior injected through a spatial gate is therefore insufficient on BRISC, and stronger prior integration, longer training and additional datasets are needed to establish any benefit.

Using the BRISC dataset of 2D contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI slices (glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor), we compare the proposed model with a vanilla U-Net and a learned-gate ablation under identical training, using 3-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set of 860 images. We evaluate Dice, IoU, precision, recall, Hausdorff distance, HD95 and a dedicated far false-positive measure. The proposed model matched the baseline in Dice (0.709 versus 0.708) and showed a slightly lower but non-significant HD95 (36.5 versus 37.9 px, p = 0.26); it did not significantly reduce far false positives (49.7 versus 48.0 px, p = 0.82). A simple location prior injected through a spatial gate is therefore insufficient on BRISC, and stronger prior integration, longer training and additional datasets are needed to establish any benefit.

title: Early Postoperative Trajectories for Six-Month Outcome Prediction after Endoscopic Sinus Surgery: A Leakage-Safe Comparison of Transformer and Conventional Machine-Learning Models
abstract: Abstract Early recovery after endoscopic sinus surgery may contain prognostic information that is not available preoperatively. We investigated whether trajectories measured through one postoperative month predict six-month outcomes in chronic rhinosinusitis and whether a trajectory-specific Transformer outperforms conventional models. This secondary analysis used 95 participants from a prospective randomized study (49 control; 46 biodegradable steroid-eluting stent). Predictors comprised baseline covariates and endoscopy, five-item visual analogue scale (VAS), and 22-item Sinonasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) measurements at baseline, two weeks, and one month. Six-month continuous outcomes were predicted using repeated nested cross-validation (10 repetitions of five folds). For six-month SNOT-22 prediction from one-month data, Extra Trees achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.044 (95% CI 1.934–2.156), compared with 2.055 (1.953–2.149) for a clinically restricted ridge model and 2.624 (2.482–2.777) for the proposed EPT-Former. EPT-Former was significantly worse than the horizon-specific best comparator at every horizon (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Adding early postoperative observations improved all principal models, but tree and regularized linear models retained an advantage. Early trajectories were informative, whereas increased architectural complexity did not improve prediction in this small structured cohort. External validation is required before clinical use.

title: Targeted delivery of streptokinase based on fibrin-specific liposomes for in vivo ultrasound catheter thrombolysis
abstract: Abstract Background Thrombolytic drugs, including streptokinase (SK), are widely used in the treatment of acute thrombosis. A new fibrin-specific immunoliposomal formulation of streptokinase (LSK) for local delivery to the thrombolytic site has demonstrated a significant increase in vascular clearance compared to native SK. Objectives To assess the feasibility of improving the efficiency of fibrin-specific liposomes for SK targeted delivery in combination with the intravascular action of catheter ultrasound (US), in acute peripheral arterial thrombosis. Methods 15 adult male mongrel dogs with arterial thrombosis induced by thrombin were divided into three groups: I) US exposure; II) SC-LSC; III) SC-LSC, followed 30 min after administration by US exposure. US frequency of 25 kHz and an intensity of 48 W/cm² was delivered to the thrombosis zone using a flexible 56 cm waveguide. Assessment of hemostatic parameters included the determination of D-dimer, fibrinogen, plasminogen, and α2-antiplasmin levels. The degree of vessel lumen patency was assessed using histological morphometry. Results An in vivo experiment demonstrated the potential to significantly enhance the thrombolytic effect of a combined thrombolytic drug comprising 60% native (molecular) SK and 40% LSK, with the additional local application of low-frequency high-intensity ultrasound. The degree of thrombolysis was greatest with the combined action of ultrasound and SK-LSK (86.1%) compared to the individual use of SK-LSK drug (70.2%) and ultrasound alone (12.3%). Conclusions The introduction of US into the thrombosis zone in combination with a thrombolytic agent containing free SK and LSK ensured a high degree of thrombolysis without causing a critical increase in fibrinogenolysis, bleeding and other dangerous consequences for animals.

title: Longitudinal Alzheimer's Disease Classification from 2.5D MRI and Clinical Data via Adaptive Gated Fusion
abstract: Abstract Reliable discrimination between cognitively stable and impaired individuals remains a clinically important challenge in Alzheimer's disease (AD) assessment. Existing multimodal deep learning approaches have predominantly relied on computationally intensive 3D convolutional networks, while relatively few studies jointly model longitudinal imaging and non-imaging data or explicitly account for patient-specific modality contributions. In this work, a multimodal longitudinal framework is proposed that combines 2.5D MRI feature extraction with bidirectional LSTM-based longitudinal sequence encoding. A residual gated fusion mechanism adaptively weights imaging and clinical features for each patient, enabling joint learning of longitudinal and multimodal representations. Structural MRI and clinical data from 204 patients across three longitudinal visits from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) were evaluated using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation to prevent information leakage across visits. The proposed framework achieved a mean AUC of 0.870 ± 0.035, balanced accuracy of 0.802, sensitivity of 0.756, and specificity of 0.847, consistently outperforming unimodal baselines and alternative architectural variants. Ablation studies demonstrated that longitudinal modeling, the 2.5D representation, and residual gated fusion each contributed independently to the overall performance. Quantitative Grad-CAM analysis further revealed cross-visit spatial consistency and significantly greater medial activation in cognitively impaired individuals than in stable individuals, indicating that the model focuses on neuroanatomically plausible regions associated with neurodegenerative change. Our work underscores the potential of multimodal longitudinal deep learning to improve AD assessment while leveraging routinely collected imaging and clinical data.

title: Successful Management of Acute SMV occlusion in Pancreatic Conversion Surgery After Carbon Ion Radiotherapy: A rare complication and surgical pitfall
abstract: Abstract Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often locally advanced at diagnosis, and multimodal strategies including conversion therapy are used to increase the chance of margin-negative resection. Carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIRT) enables strong local tumor control. However, the side effect of CIRT toward local vasculature has not yet been fully understood. Literatures regarding the surgical pitfall of vessel reconstruction after CIRT have barely been reported. Case presentation: A 45-year-old female initially diagnosed with locally advanced PDAC underwent 14 cycles of systemic chemotherapy followed by CIRT. After conversion, she underwent distal pancreatectomy with common hepatic artery divestment. Superior mesenteric vein (SMV) was partially trimmed due to dense adhesion between pancreas, resulting in a 1.5cm defect. The defect was repaired primarily with 5 − 0 Prolene suture. On postoperative day2, she developed high fever and rapid deterioration of liver function. Urgent contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated critical narrowing/near-occlusion of portal vein/SMV without definite thrombus. Emergent exploratory laparotomy showed severe intimal fibrosis of SMV causing luminal compromise. The SMV defect was reconstructed using patch augmentation. The patient achieved an R0 resection with final pathological finding revealing residual ductal adenocarcinoma in a fibrotic background (pT1b pN0). Her Liver function rapidly recovered after the venous reconstruction. Conclusions: This case shows a rare post-CIRT vascular complication with SMV to portal vein fibrosis causing acute hepatic ischemia after pancreatic cancer conversion surgery, which was successfully rescued with prompt patch augmentation. To avoid such complications in conversion surgery for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC), it is of crucial importance to take radiation-related vasculopathy into consideration during the manipulation of vasculature nearby to the previously CIRT-radiated area.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D Local Fibre Orientation Estimation in Composite Computed Tomography: From Volumetric Convolutions to Real-Time Direct Projection Inversion
abstract: Abstract The mechanical integrity, load-bearing efficiency, and damage tolerance of short- and continuous-fiber-reinforced polymer (SFRP/CFRP) composites depend intrinsically on their local 3D fiber-orientation distribution. While X-ray micro-computed tomography (μCT) non-destructively reveals microstructural morphology, standard volumetric extraction relies on classical 3D structure-tensor eigen-analysis. These classical approaches require dense angular projection sets (180+ views), computationally demanding Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions, manual filter tuning, and exhibit severe degradation under Poisson photon noise. This paper introduces an end-to-end deep learning framework for local fiber orientation estimation that operates across two practical regimes: high-precision offline volumetric inspection and real-time inline scan-to-orientation inspection. To overcome the scarcity of physical CT ground truth, we develop a physics-grounded synthetic pipeline coupling directional sampling via the von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distribution (κ∈[0.5,25]) with collision-free Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) packing (V_f∈[10%,35%]) and GPU-accelerated forward projection with realistic Poisson noise. Ground truth is formulated analytically through second-order orientation tensors, mathematically resolving the unoriented fiber director ±180^∘ sign ambiguity. We benchmark three paradigms across N=7,889 held-out sub-volume patches drawn from 150 independent composite phantoms (70/15/15 parent split): (1) classical 3D structure tensor eigen-analysis, (2) a 3D volumetric convolutional neural network (Model B), and (3) a novel Direct Projection Network (Model C) that infers 3D orientation directly from only 8 raw 2D sinogram projection views, completely bypassing 3D volumetric reconstruction. Model B achieves an overall mean angular error of 9.35 ∘ (4.78 ∘ on aligned tape; a 67% error reduction relative to the 28.27 ∘ classical baseline) at an inference throughput of 140.9 patches/s on GPU. Model C demonstrates that 3D orientation can be recovered directly from sparse 2D projection shadows with 22.57 ∘ overall error (11.35 ∘ on aligned composites), achieving 174.0 patches/s with zero reconstruction computational overhead. Furthermore, industrial tolerance evaluation demonstrates an 84.57% in-spec acceptance rate at automotive tolerance (τ≤15^∘) for Model B. This work demonstrates that deep learning provides both a superior offline alternative to classical image filtering and a viable pathway for inline, reconstruction-free composite manufacturing quality assurance.

title: MedCapVQA: A Two-Stage Explainable Framework for Medical Visual Question Answering
abstract: Abstract Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) aims to answer natural language questions about clinical images and has significant potential for diagnostic support, medical education, and improved access to expert interpretation. Most Med-VQA systems fuse image features and question embeddings directly, a mapping that is hard to learn from the few thousand question--answer pairs that medical benchmarks provide and that is usually compensated for with large-scale domain pre-training. We propose \modelname{}, a two-stage, caption-driven framework that describes the image first and answers the question second. A MedGemma captioner, adapted with parameter-efficient fine-tuning on ROCOv2, converts each medical image into a clinically meaningful caption; a BioBERT-based reasoner with dedicated caption and question encoders and question-to-caption cross-attention then predicts the answer from text alone. We evaluate \modelname{} on the closed-ended questions of the VQA-Med 2019 benchmark, training on the official training set (3,200 medical images, 12,792 question--answer pairs) and evaluating on the official validation set (500 images, 2,000 question--answer pairs), against six baselines that represent the main prior design families: a convolutional--recurrent fusion model, BioBERT and Med3D domain-adapted variants, a self-attention fusion network, a Vision Transformer model with cross-attention, and an end-to-end fine-tuned vision-language model. All models are trained under the same protocol and across training-set proportions from 5\% to 100\%, with each data-size result averaged over ten random training subsets. \modelname{} achieves the highest validation accuracy on both tasks: 81.9\% on binary (yes/no) questions, 11.6 percentage points above the strongest baseline, and 73.9\% on 71-category multiclass questions, 5.4 points above the fine-tuned vision-language model and 13.5 points above the Vision Transformer model. The vision-language model attains a higher multiclass training accuracy but lower validation accuracy compared to \modelname{} and none of the baseline models are strong on both tasks. The \modelname{} reasoner trains on a single GPU in $\sim$5 hours. These results show that converting medical images into textual captions before reasoning is an effective and resource-efficient alternative to direct multimodal fusion, and they highlight the value of intermediate semantic representations for the design of next-generation Med-VQA systems.

title: Daily CBCT-Based Repeated-Measures Analysis of Setup Reproducibility and Treatment-Course Stability of Three Positioning–Immobilization Strategies in Cervical Cancer VMAT
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate and reproducible patient positioning is essential for image-guided radiotherapy (IGRT) in cervical cancer. This study compared pretreatment setup reproducibility and treatment-course changes among three positioning–immobilization strategies using daily cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and repeated-measures analysis. Methods This retrospective study included 255 patients undergoing volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) for cervical cancer: Group A, supine positioning with vacuum-cushion immobilization (n = 100); Group B, prone positioning with an Orfit body frame and thermoplastic fixation (n = 100); and Group C, prone positioning with an individualized belly-board system (n = 55). A total of 6,255 daily pretreatment CBCT registrations were analyzed. Pre-correction translational setup deviations in the longitudinal (LNG), lateral (LAT), and vertical (VRT) directions and the corresponding three-dimensional (3D) vector magnitude were evaluated. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) models accounted for within-patient correlation, with multivariable adjustment for age, body mass index, and irradiation field extent. Patient-level sensitivity analyses, descriptive setup-related uncertainty estimates, and threshold-based reproducibility analyses requiring simultaneous attainment in all three translational directions were also performed. Results In adjusted GEE analysis, 3D vector magnitude was greater in Group B (β = 0.0647 cm; 95% CI, 0.0077–0.1217; P = 0.026) and Group C (β = 0.1038 cm; 95% CI, 0.0342–0.1734; P = 0.003) than in Group A. Treatment fraction number was positively associated with 3D vector magnitude (β = 0.0032 cm/fraction; P < 0.001), without significant group-by-fraction interactions. Patient-level sensitivity analyses supported the overall between-group pattern. Direction-specific analyses showed greater longitudinal deviations in Group B and greater vertical deviations in Group C. Under the strict patient-level criterion requiring all three absolute directional deviations to remain ≤ 0.5 cm at every available CBCT verification, attainment rates were 43.0%, 28.0%, and 12.7% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (P < 0.001). Conclusions The three positioning–immobilization strategies exhibited distinct patterns of pre-correction setup deviations during daily CBCT-guided VMAT for cervical cancer. Supine positioning with vacuum-cushion immobilization was associated with smaller 3D setup deviations and higher descriptive threshold-attainment rates than the two prone strategies in this cohort. These findings reflect pretreatment setup reproducibility rather than isolated immobilization-device performance, post-correction treatment accuracy, or recommended clinical planning margins. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study was a retrospective observational analysis of routinely collected clinical data. No prospective assignment of participants to study-related interventions was performed.

title: AI-Based Particle Size Distribution Prediction from 3D Packed-Particle Tomographic Volumes: A Comparative Study with classical Watershed Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Abstract Determining the Particle Size Distribution (PSD) of granular media and powder compacts is vital across condensed matter physics, geological sciences, and materials engineering. While X-ray computed tomography (µCT) captures granular microstructure non-destructively, traditional quantitative PSD estimation relies on classical morphological segmentation (binarization, distance transform, and watershed flooding), which is computationally intensive and sensitive to contact-neck ambiguities. In this work, we investigate whether a compact 3D Convolutional Neural Network (Compact3DCNN, 300,900 parameters) can predict normalized 20-bin PSD histograms directly from unsegmented 3D grayscale volumes without intermediate particle instance extraction. Using a synthetic dataset of 60 independent non-overlapping polydisperse packed-sphere volumes (48 3 voxels) with exact analytic PSD ground truth, we benchmark the CNN against a classical 3D Euclidean distance-transform watershed baseline on an untouched, held-out test split (N = 10, 40 train / 10 validation / 10 test). On this low-to-moderate packing regime (15%–25%), the classical watershed baseline achieved superior accuracy, attaining a mean Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) of 0.0974 ± 0.0261 voxels compared to 0.3428 ± 0.0949 voxels for the CNN (paired 95% bootstrap CI: [+0.1837, +0.3156] voxels). Measured runtime was 1.19 ± 0.27 ms per volume for the CNN on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU versus 33.71 ± 7.50 ms for the watershed pipeline on an Intel CPU; however, we emphasize that this reflects disparate computing architectures rather than a controlled hardware comparison. Furthermore, comparison against an empirical training-set-mean baseline (0.6206 ± 0.2440 vx EMD on validation) confirms that the CNN learns volume-specific morphological features (0.3970 ± 0.1335 vx, a 36.0% error reduction). A controlled validation experiment evaluating direct 1D Wasserstein-1 loss training yielded substantially higher error (1.1382 ± 0.4907 vx EMD) than the primary Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence configuration, illustrating optimization challenges in cumulative L1 histogram penalties. Our findings characterize the accuracy-throughput profile in direct volumetric PSD regression and delineate key open challenges for dense granular systems.

A controlled validation experiment evaluating direct 1D Wasserstein-1 loss training yielded substantially higher error (1.1382 ± 0.4907 vx EMD) than the primary Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence configuration, illustrating optimization challenges in cumulative L1 histogram penalties. Our findings characterize the accuracy-throughput profile in direct volumetric PSD regression and delineate key open challenges for dense granular systems.

title: Final survival analysis and predictors of treatment discontinuation in patients aged ≥ 80 years receiving adjuvant uracil–tegafur and leucovorin for stage III colorectal cancer: The prospective phase II HiSCO-03 trial
abstract: Abstract Background In the HiSCO-03 trial of adjuvant uracil–tegafur and leucovorin in patients aged ≥ 80 years with stage III colorectal cancer, the treatment completion rate was lower than expected. This final analysis evaluated long-term outcomes and risk factors for treatment discontinuation. Methods Of 69 enrolled patients, 65 were included in the survival analysis. In exploratory analyses, skeletal muscle mass was measured on preoperative computed tomography at the third lumbar vertebra, and risk factors for discontinuation due to adverse events or patient refusal were analyzed using logistic regression in 45 patients, excluding those who discontinued treatment because of recurrence. Results The 3-year disease-free survival rate was 70.6%, and the 5-year overall, recurrence-free, and disease-free survival rates were 75.9%, 64.5%, and 61.4%, respectively. Of the 45 patients, 30 completed and 15 discontinued treatment. In multivariable analysis, female sex (odds ratio 7.75, 95% confidence interval 1.68–56.59) and low skeletal muscle mass (odds ratio 9.69, 95% confidence interval 1.84–78.11) were independent risk factors for discontinuation. Survival did not differ between patients who completed and those who discontinued treatment. Conclusions In patients aged ≥ 80 years with stage III colorectal cancer, adjuvant uracil–tegafur and leucovorin achieved a 3-year disease-free survival rate comparable to those reported in younger patients. Low skeletal muscle mass and female sex were associated with treatment discontinuation. These factors may help identify, before treatment, patients who are likely to tolerate adjuvant chemotherapy and those who need early supportive care. Trial registration jRCTs061180087 (registered 22 March 2019 retrospectively registered).

title: A multicentre longitudinal brain metastasis imaging dataset with lesion segmentations and clinical data
abstract: Abstract Brain metastases exhibit substantial variability in lesion burden, morphology and treatment response. Longitudinal imaging linked to lesion annotations and clinical histories can support quantitative studies of this heterogeneity. We describe a multicentre dataset from seven Spanish hospitals comprising 443 patients diagnosed between 2007 and 2022, with follow-up imaging for 216 patients. The collection contains 2842 magnetic resonance image, including 1092 three dimensional (3D) contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, 833 T2-weighted and 917 FLAIR (fluid-attenuated inversion recovery) images. Semiautomatic 3D-segmentation with expert review provides annotations for 1291 unique lesions represented by 2303 lesion observations across imaging time points. Separate labels identify contrast-enhancing and non-enhancing or necrotic tumour components, and lesion identifiers are maintained during follow-up. Accompanying records describe primary tumour characteristics, treatments, imaging dates and clinical outcomes, together with acquisition metadata and 107 morphological and radiomic features. The dataset supports research on lesion detection and segmentation, longitudinal response assessment, imaging biomarkers and mathematical models of brain metastasis growth and treatment response.
